_comment: KATOMIA-CONFIG1 (2026-07-14): site-wide, non-secret config. Not build/deploy secrets — deliberately git-tracked (see .gitignore's narrow negation of the blanket *.json rule for this one file) so it's administrable/reviewable like any other code. Lives inside m/katomia/ on purpose: the user wants everything Katomia-related self-contained in this one folder so a future white-label deploy (a separate site, its own config) or a relocation/bundle only ever has to carry this folder. Extend this file (not a second one) for future site-wide settings — default skin, branding, etc.

terms._comment: ENTRY-CIRCLES1 (user 2026-07-30): the user-facing name for the space people meet in is a PARAMETER, not a hardcoded word. Internally it stays a 'proposal' game (tradingMode:proposal) — that name is untouched and remains the code/API vocabulary. Only the display word changes. Why: the same product is pitched differently per audience — 'circle' for the launch/community framing (non-hierarchical, organic, matches the liquidity/bubble branding), but 'game' when playful, or 'market'/'boardroom' for a business or white-label deploy where hippy language would land badly. 'Ring' was rejected by the user this day: it reads as a fight, or worse. Change the four forms here and every surface follows. Any string in this file may use {one}/{One}/{many}/{Many} placeholders; katomiaTerm()/katomiaTermFill() in site-config.php do the substitution, and window.KTERMS exposes them to JS.

landing._curatedNote: ENTRY-CIRCLES1 R1 (user 2026-07-30): say plainly what each one is — 'Testnet Circle' / 'Mainnet Circle' — with the flavour demoted to muted note text. The launch audience is Hedera users who know exactly what testnet and mainnet mean; inventing cute names for them only obscures it. Dropped 'Practice/Open Ring': 'ring' reads as a fight, and 'practice' is wrong because people may play for real on testnet AND practise on mainnet (there are play tokens there) — that split is not cleanly defined, so don't imply it. 🟠/🟣 mirror HashScan's network colours and the network chips already in contents.php (and note the circle-emoji convention bars circles in PLAYER names, not network chips). UNRESOLVED (user, same day): whether the titles stay literal or return to flavour names, and whether the emoji stay as network dots or become something play-flavoured — a test tube was rejected because labs environments exist on mainnet too.
